subject: BLOCK CONTAINS clause
notes: Printed format: BLOCK [CONTAINS] [integer-1 TO] integer-2 {[CHARACTERS] | RECORDS} (BLOCK/TO/RECORDS underlined; CONTAINS and CHARACTERS optional words, so omitting the unit word = CHARACTERS). Grammar: BLOCK CONTAINS? integerLiteral (TO integerLiteral)? (CHARACTERS | RECORDS)? - exact. Placement: fileDescriptionClause alternative (FD only; SD excluded per sortMergeDescriptionEntry). Probed pinned cobol.exe at --std 85 and 2023: 'BLOCK CONTAINS 2 RECORDS', 'BLOCK 100', 'BLOCK CONTAINS 10 TO 100 CHARACTERS', 'BLOCK CONTAINS 10 TO 20' all compile and run; '+5' and '5.5' refused (COBOL0001, integer-n required); 'CHARACTERS RECORDS' refused (COBOL0307, braces choose one); zero refused COBOL2386 (§5.5 1) nonzero default). conformance:cases/11.2-Identification-division-structure/pb829_closed_formats_legal exercises only the 'BLOCK CONTAINS 1 RECORDS' arm, so it is not a covering test for the whole format -> test-ref empty. cite.py --check 13.18.10.1 "The BLOCK CONTAINS clause specifies the size of a physical record." -> OK. || Editions (adjudicator): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (clause present unchanged in every edition; Annex E records no change to 13.18.10)
